newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - GRETZKY HAS FOUR ASSISTS AS RANGERS BEAT WHALERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - GRETZKY HAS FOUR ASSISTS AS RANGERS BEAT WHALERS.

text.p: The Hartford Whalers tried to get rough with Wayne Gretzky Wednesday, but he made them pay.
Gretzky had four assists, Luc Robitaille had two goals and an assist and Adam Graves scored twice as the Rangers stopped a four-game home winless streak with a 5-2 victory over the slumping Whalers.

"They took some liberties on me tonight, but it's been done to me before," said Gretzky, who has 18 assists in his last 14 games. "There comes a time when you get frustrated, but you just try to channel your energy in a positive way."
"You have to be physical with the Rangers, you can't let them skate freely and at times tonight we gave them too much room," Hartford coach Paul Maurice said.
The Rangers improved to 4-3-1 in their last eight games overall and 1-3-1 in their last five at Madison Square Garden.
Brian Leetch had the other New York goal while former Ranger Steven Rice and Hnat Domenichelli tallied for Hartford.
In Montreal, Glenn Murray scored two goals in a 3:02 span of the third period and Jarmoir Jagr added his league-leading 44th tally as the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Canadiens 6-3.

Despite playing without centre Mario Lemieux, who sat out with back spasms one day after becoming the seventh player in NHL history to score 600 goals, the Penguins improved to 13-2-1 in their last 16 road games. In Lemieux's last visit to Montreal, he scored four goals in the third period.

Petr Nedved added two power-play goals and rookie Patrick Lalime continued to stake his claim to the Calder Trophy, stopping 46 shots. Lalime is 18-2-2 since being called up from the International Hockey League.
Stu Barnes scored Pittsburgh's first goal while Martin Rucinsky, Vladimir Malakhov and Mark Recchi tallied for Montreal.

Valeri Bure and Vincent Damphousse had two assists apiece for the Canadiens, who outshot Pittsburgh 49-34. Montreal had a three-game unbeaten streak stopped and lost at home to the Penguins for the second time in 10 days.
In Dallas, Arturs Irbe stopped 28 shots for his first shutout of the season and four different players scored goals, leading the Stars to a 4-0 victory over the punchless Tampa Bay Lightning.

Irbe, signed by Dallas as a free agent in the off-season, made 10 saves in the first period and nine in both the second and third for his ninth career shutout. Irbe evened his season record at 7-7-1 in his 200th career game.

Dave Reid scored in the first period and Pat Verbeek, Joe Nieuwendyk and Neal Broten tallied in the third period for Dallas, which lengthened its lead over second-place Detroit in the Central Division to six points.
Rick Tabaracci turned away 27 shots for Tampa Bay, which has lost five of its last six games, scoring only eight goals in that span.
In Edmonton, red-hot Curtis Joseph made 31 saves and Doug Weight scored twice as the Oilers scored five unanswered goals for their fifth straight win, 5-2 over the Calgary Flames.
Edmonton has won eight of its last nine home games and five straight overall. Joseph has allowed just five goals during the streak.
Jason Arnott, Todd Marchant and Mariusz Czerkawski also tallied for Edmonton.
German Titov and Tommy Albelin tallied for the Flames, who have lost three of their last four games.
In New Jersey, Martin Brodeur made 25 saves and Steve Sullivan had a goal and an assist as the Devils continued their home mastery of the New York Islanders with a 4-1 win.

Bill Guerin, Randy McKay and Dave Andreychuk also tallied and Bobby Holik had a pair of assists for New Jersey, which is 8-0-1 in its last nine home games against the Islanders. The Devils improved to 2-0-3 in their last five games overall.
Brodeur allowed only Bryan Smolinski's second-period power-play goal.

In San Jose, Ron Sutter's first power-play goal of the season with 4:35 left in the third period snapped a tie as the Sharks rallied from a two-goal deficit for a 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Bernie Nicholls assisted on all three goals for the Sharks, who have won three of their last four games and all three meetings with Los Angeles this season.
In Toronto, Mats Sundin scored twice and Doug Gilmour set up three goals, helping the Maple Leafs end a five-game winless streak with a 4-2 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
Jamie Baker and Mathieu Schneider also scored for Toronto, which had been 0-4-1 in its last five games.
Paul Kariya and Teemu Selanne tallied for Anaheim, which has lost three straight games and four of its last five.
